transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for having me, I really appreciate you taking the time. Um, well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble at work lately. 

I work at a dry cleaner's, and I really try my best to do a good job, I promise I do. But... I just can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly. The tickets, the receipts, my little workshop notes, the customer jobs... they all just sort of end up piled together on me. And then I just look at it all and I don't know what to handle first. 

I'm sure it sounds silly, and I really don't want my boss to think I'm slacking off, because I'm definitely not. Is... is that the kind of thing you can help with? I just want to get back to doing a good job.
Has this kind of trouble staying organized and focused been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this a new change that started more recently?

Oh, um... well, I guess it's not entirely new. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I've always been a mess or anything, because I really do try hard to be good! But, um... if I think back to when I was little, I suppose I did have some similar trouble. 

Even in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother that I was a bright girl, which was nice of them to say, but... they also said I was a bit, well, scattered. I guess I was always talking out of turn a little bit, or losing my worksheets. And they had to remind me a lot to actually finish what I was doing. I always meant well, though! I just... got a little off track sometimes. Is it okay that I'm bringing up things from that long ago? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.

When you find yourself unable to keep your tasks organized, do you also notice a lot of persistent worry or anxious feelings about work or other things, or is it more that your mind just drifts and you get distracted without necessarily feeling worried?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier. I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? I definitely don't want you to think I'm sitting at the counter panicking or... or letting my nerves get the best of me. I really do try to stay cheerful for the customers. 

It's really more of the second thing you said. My mind just sort of... floats away. I'll be looking right at a dry cleaning ticket, and then suddenly I'm thinking about what I need to pick up at the grocery store, or... or I'll notice a loose button on a coat across the room. I don't feel scared or anxious when it happens, I just... I drift off, and before I know it, I've completely lost my place. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that the right way. I just don't want to make it sound like I'm a nervous wreck, because I'm really not!

Aside from losing track of tasks, do you often feel physically restless, fidgety, or find yourself acting or speaking impulsively—like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Oh, goodness... well, I really try my best to be polite, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm rude or... or bossy with the people I work with, because I really do love my staff! 

But, um... I suppose I do have a little bit of a habit of jumping in sometimes. Like, if they're having a conversation, I might accidentally cut into it without meaning to. Or... well, sometimes if I see them sorting the clothes at the front, I just reach right over and start fixing how they're doing it before they even ask me for help. 

I just want everything to be perfect for the customers, you know? But I know it comes off like I'm butting in, and I always feel a little bad about it right after I do it. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person to work with... is that what you meant by acting without thinking?
Do you often feel physically restless at work—like needing to get up and move around, fidgeting with your hands, or finding it hard to stay seated or still for long periods?

Oh, um... well, I don't want to make it seem like I can't behave myself when I'm supposed to. I really try to be respectful when people are talking! But, um... I guess I do have a little bit of trouble just staying put sometimes. 

Like, when we have our church committee meetings, or... or even those fabric-care training seminars for work, I always seem to be the one getting up. I'll suddenly realize I need a glass of water, or I'll remember a piece of paper I left in the other room, or I'll just need to go check on something real quick. And then I'll look around and notice that everyone else has just been sitting perfectly still the whole time. 

I always try to be really quiet about it so I don't bother anyone! I just... I get this feeling like I need to stretch my legs a bit. Is that okay? I mean, I hope that doesn't make me sound like a disruption to the group.
